remaining_concerns: The policy requires material weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance before certification, and no such current-release artifact was provided.
The available evidence still shows the loan modification support slice is 1.4 percentage points below the warning threshold in the current release.
The record still contains only an informal post-launch monitoring comment, not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to a weak, caveated certification theory based on the same record. That reframing is analytically more careful, but it does not satisfy the policy predicate. The governing policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence still shows a current subgroup regression for a named launch use case, plus only an informal monitoring note with no reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness in part, but they do not cure the unresolved disclosure/approval requirement. Because no initial concern was closed by genuinely new admissible evidence, the case remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats. A caveated argument can narrow an overbroad claim, but here the caveat itself marks an unmet compliance condition, not a resolved one.
